profile.address: 8851 South Sandy Parkway, Sandy City, UT 84070
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged simply Verizon, sits in Sandy City, Salt Lake County, Utah. The address itself carries a documented discrepancy: an earlier version of the OSM way recorded house number 8871, which a later edit sourced to the Esri National Address Database import changed to 8851 South Sandy Parkway, Sandy City, Utah 84070. That kind of correction is common when authoritative address databases are merged into OpenStreetMap and does not by itself cast doubt on the site identification, but it means the exact street number carries some documented uncertainty. More significant is the provenance of the telecom=data_center classification itself: the tag was added through a MapRoulette editing task, a gamified crowdsourced mapping platform where contributors work through externally generated candidate lists of features to verify, and the changeset comment reads only added a datacenter to the map with a MapRoulette task reference, with no indication the contributor visited the site, consulted a business filing, or verified the classification against any primary source. This is the weakest tag provenance found anywhere in this Verizon record cluster, suggesting the mapper was working off a pre-existing external list of candidate locations rather than confirming this specific site. Utah is outside the nine-state footprint where Verizon operates as the legacy incumbent local exchange carrier, so a regional Bell heritage explanation does not apply, and no operator fact sheet, county property record, or trade-press source confirming an active Verizon facility at this address was located this session. This record should be read as an unverified crowdsourced tag on a real company name rather than a confirmed data center, and no capacity, square footage, tier, or year-built figures are asserted.

sources.title: Equinix Completes Acquisition of 29 Data Centers from Verizon

profile.research_note: Verizon sold its commercial colocation/data-center business (29 facilities) to Equinix in 2017 and exited the public colocation market; it does not publish colocation spec sheets. These rows are Verizon-operated network facilities (switching centers, wireless MSC/central-office buildings) rather than for-lease colocation space, and no public technical spec page exists for them. Marked specs_unpublished rather than guess.
sources_tried: A Baxtel listing whose own title names South Sandy and gives a specific street address consistent with this registrys own Sandy City label

reading.body:
No published technical specifications exist for this facility. Verizon exited the commercial colocation business in 2017, selling 29 data centers to Equinix, and does not publish capacity or power figures for its network switching centers and wireless infrastructure buildings. This record originated from a crowdsourced mapping platform where a contributor tagged the address without documented verification against primary sources, business filings, or on-site confirmation.

The site carries unresolved address uncertainty and no confirmation beyond a real company name applied to a real street address in Sandy City. Utah lies outside Verizon's legacy regional footprint as an incumbent local exchange carrier, and no operator fact sheet, county property record, or trade press source confirmed an active facility at this location during research.

This campus should not be counted as published AI infrastructure capacity. Utah has 21 mapped data center facilities, of which only 9 report published megawatts totaling 52.18 MW across the state. A facility with no specs, no verification, and no capacity claim cannot inform decisions about grid binding constraints on AI scaling, regardless of its rank in an unverified inventory.
